summary: The same HTTP assertion test passes in the intended iDFlakies order and fails in the revealed order, where a max-size test runs before it; the record classifies the failure as order-dependent.
root_cause: The tests share one JVM-wide configuration map. Each test instance takes its world from the static SingletonObjectFactory holder and therefore resolves the same @Singleton GlobalWorld, whose context map is built once on injection and is never reset between tests. The preceding test writes ASSERTS_STATUS_CODE_MAX_SIZE=5 and never clears it. The victim enables body display but never sets or clears that key, so it inherits the leaked limit, and the sibling tests in the same class establish that such a limit yields the truncated assertion text rather than the full body the victim expects. The outcome therefore depends on the order in which the tests run.
recommended_action: Reset or reconstruct the shared GlobalWorld between tests, or make every test establish and clean up each configuration key it depends on instead of inheriting state from earlier tests.
